root_cause.text: The ALSA firewire-motu hwdep_read() loop copied DSP events as fixed 4-byte u32 values with put_user() without verifying that the remaining user buffer space was at least sizeof(ev), so non-4-byte-aligned count values caused an out-of-bounds user-buffer write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (put_user(ev, ptr))` to `if (consumed + sizeof(ev) > count || put_user(ev, ptr))` in `sound/firewire/motu/motu-hwdep.c`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that when the user buffer size is not aligned to 4 bytes, the put_user() loop could overwrite beyond the buffer boundary.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a size boundary check before copying each DSP event to userspace so reads do not overrun the requested count.
intent_record.what: The condition inside the read loop was changed from only checking `put_user(ev, ptr)` to first checking `consumed + sizeof(ev) > count` and then `put_user(ev, ptr)`, returning `-EFAULT` if either condition is true.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from copying a DSP event to userspace when there is not enough remaining space in the requested byte count, avoiding a partial or out-of-bounds write attempt and ensuring only whole events are emitted within the caller-provided limit.

grouping_result.intent: Add a size boundary check before copying each DSP event to userspace so reads do not overrun the requested count.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by checking remaining buffer space before copying each 4-byte DSP event to userspace, preventing overruns when count is not aligned to sizeof(ev).

candidates.rationale: This performs the 4-byte userspace write for each DSP event without first verifying that at least sizeof(ev) bytes remain in the user-requested buffer, directly enabling an out-of-bounds write when count is not 4-byte aligned.
The loop condition only checks consumed < count, not whether count - consumed is at least sizeof(ev), so it allows another iteration even when fewer than 4 bytes remain.
This computes a u32 userspace destination at the current offset regardless of whether 4 writable bytes remain, setting up the subsequent out-of-bounds put_user().

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the actual 4-byte copy of a DSP event to userspace. Because the code did not first ensure that at least sizeof(ev) bytes remained in the user buffer, this write could overrun the requested count when count was not 4-byte aligned.

This loop condition allowed another iteration whenever any bytes remained, but did not require that at least a full 4-byte event fit. That insufficient bounds check enabled the subsequent put_user() call to write past the requested user-buffer length.

This computes a u32-aligned userspace destination for a 4-byte write at the current offset without verifying that 4 bytes remain available in the user buffer, directly setting up the out-of-bounds put_user() write.

The vulnerable construct is present in the new branch: `else if (snd_motu_register_dsp_message_parser_count_event(motu) > 0) { ... }`. Inside it, the code reserves header space with `consumed += sizeof(event.motu_register_dsp_change);` and then loops with `while (consumed < count && snd_motu_register_dsp_message_parser_copy_event(motu, &ev)) { ptr = (u32 __user *)(buf + consumed); if (put_user(ev, ptr)) return -EFAULT; consumed += sizeof(ev); }`. The root cause is that the loop condition checks only `consumed < count`, but each iteration writes a fixed 4-byte `u32` via `put_user(ev, ptr)`. There is no check that the remaining user buffer space is at least `sizeof(ev)` (for example, `count - consumed >= sizeof(ev)`). Therefore, if `count` is not 4-byte aligned and only 1-3 bytes remain, the loop still performs a 4-byte write past the end of the requested user buffer. The later header write `copy_to_user(buf, &event, sizeof(event.motu_register_dsp_change))` does not fix this issue. Hence this commit introduces the buggy logic and does not yet contain the fix.
